rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The turning effect of a force is its **moment (torque)**: τ = F × d, with d the perpendicular distance from the axis to the force's line of action — the reason door handles sit far from hinges and a force through the pivot turns nothing.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - τ = F × d (d = perpendicular distance); vector τ⃗ = r⃗ × F⃗ - Equilibrium: ΣF⃗ = 0 and Στ⃗ = 0 - Couple torque: F × separation

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Torque vs work:** both N·m dimensionally, but torque is a vector turning effect (N·m, not joules) while work is scalar energy transfer (joules).  ·  **Centre of mass vs centre of gravity:** identical in uniform gravity; the centre of gravity is where weight's moment acts.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A light beam means its weight is neglected.  ·  Couple: two equal opposite forces with different lines of action, net force zero, net torque not zero.

rows.label: Solved

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A uniform 200 N ladder of 5 m rests against a smooth wall at 60° to the ground. Find the wall's reaction.** — Taking moments about the foot: N_wall × 5 sin 60° = 200 × 2.5 cos 60° → N_wall = (500 × 0.5)/(5 × 0.866) = 57.7 N; the ground supplies the friction balancing it.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The moment arm rules:** a small force with a long arm beats a large force with a short one — the entire technology of levers.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Torque τ = F × d (perpendicular distance); unit N·m.  ·  Equilibrium: ΣF = 0 (translational) and Στ = 0 (rotational).  ·  Principle of moments: clockwise moments = anticlockwise moments.  ·  Couple: equal/opposite/parallel forces → pure rotation, pivot-independent torque.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Archimedes' lever claim — "give me a place to stand" — is the principle of moments stated as ambition.

rows.label: MCQ drill

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Why Handles Are Long and Seesaws Balance Force alone does not describe turning: the same 20 N opens a door easily at the handle and barely at the hinge. The turning effect is the **moment (torque)**, and its balance — the **principle of moments** — explains seesaws, levers, beam balances and every statics problem.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts | Term | Definition | Formula | Unit | |---|---|---|---| | **Moment of force (torque)** | Turning effect = force × perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action | $\tau = F \times d$ (vector: $\vec\tau = \vec r \times \vec F$) | N·m | | **Moment arm (lever arm)** | Perpendicular distance from the pivot to the force's line of action | $d$…  ·  ## 3. Why the Position of Force Matters Torque depends on the **perpendicular** distance, not the actual distance: a force applied at an angle contributes $F d\sin\theta$. This is why: - Door handles sit far from hinges (maximum moment arm). - Spanners are long; cheater bars extend them. - A force along the line through the pivot (d = 0) produces **no torque**.…
